title: Strings and template literals
learningObjectives: Explain strings and template literals and write predictable JavaScript code using the concept.

understand.concept: Strings represent text and can be written with single quotes, double quotes, or backticks. Template literals use backticks and support interpolation with ${expression} and multi-line strings. Strings are immutable; string methods return new strings rather than changing the original.
understand.whyItMatters: Template literals improve readability when combining values and text. Understanding immutability helps avoid expecting a method to modify the original string in place.
understand.analogy: A template literal is a sentence with labelled blanks that JavaScript fills with expression values.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript values, scope, and runtime behaviour follow the language specification.

explain.narrative: The template literal inserts the learner and completed values into the sentence.

examples.explanation: The template literal inserts the learner and completed values into the sentence.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser page or developer console shows the values and behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Create a multi-line template literal that reports a learner's name, course, and progress. Compare it with string concatenation.
practise.independentTask: Write a short program that uses the concept in a realistic learning-app example. Inspect values and errors in the console.
hints: Prefer const unless reassignment is required.
Do not expose private data in console output.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Strings and template literals</title></head><body>
<script>const learner='Asha';const completed=3;const message=`${learner} completed ${completed} lessons.`;console.log(message);</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which characters are used to delimit a template literal?
questions.explanation: Template literals are enclosed in backticks.

questions.prompt: What should a learner do when a JavaScript value behaves unexpectedly?
options: Assume every variable has a fixed type
